newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Stals says jobs statement based on facts.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Stals says jobs statement based on facts.

text.p: The Reserve Bank's criticism of the Basic Conditions of Employment bill was in no way a declaration of policy, Monday's Beeld newspaper quoted governor Chris Stals as saying.

Stals was responding to criticism of the central bank's statement on the bill in its latest Quarterly Bulletin, which was slammed by the ruling African National Congress (ANC) and the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) -- South Africa's largest labour federation.

"The bank speaks neither for nor against the Basic Conditions of Employment bill. (The Quarterly Bulletin) is a factual statement by an economist about what would happen if labour costs rise because of the bill," Stals said.
He said the assessment was both factual and impartial.

The bulletin, published late on Thursday, highlighted the inability of the economy to generate enough jobs to absorb South Africa's unemployed and went on to question the impact of the the Basic Conditions of Employment bill, published in April.

The Bank said that implementation of proposals including a shorter working week, increased leave arrangements, a higher premium for overtime and a training levy could have an adverse impact on formal-sector employment.
The ANC said the statement amounted to intervention in policy-making, while Cosatu said the central bank's stance showed it sided with business in the debate over the new labour policy.
